Renal ultrasound Renal ultrasound reveals small kidneys bilaterally, which indicates irreversible 
renal disease (9 and 10 cm, right and left, respectively). Only a renal biopsy could actually confirm 
the diagnosis of CGN, but it is not done once small kidneys are identified since no treatment can 
reverse kidney damage. CD’s significantly increased serum phosphate and decreased serum calcium 
levels suggest that the GFR is less than 30 mL/min, indicating significant renal dysfunction. Tests 
to eliminate other possible causes of CGN include.
